lines: Five gate stretchers, each turning a trigger into a gate of up to 10 seconds set by a knob and a CV input
A rising edge starts a gate at that channel's output, and an edge arriving during a gate restarts it at the length set then
Adds to the knob to set that channel's gate length, one volt per second, with the sum clamped to 0-10 seconds
Sets that channel's gate length in seconds, from 0 to 10 seconds, before the CV input is added to it
Carries a 10V gate that starts on the trigger and lasts for the length set for that channel
Note — each display shows that channel's current gate length in seconds.
A large mute button for a stereo pair, fading the signal down rather than cutting it
Mutes both channels on one click and unmutes them on the next, fading over a few milliseconds either way; it reads MUTE in red while sound is passing and UNMUTE in green while muted
The left signal to be muted
The right signal to be muted
Carries the left input, faded to silence while muted
Carries the right input, faded to silence while muted
Seven fixed voltages, for offsetting, biasing or testing a patch
A constant 10V
A constant 5V
A constant 1V
A constant 0V
A constant -1V
A constant -5V
A constant -10V
A blank panel whose colour is set by three CV inputs, read either as red, green and blue or as hue, saturation and lightness
Sets the red of the panel colour in RGB mode, or its hue in HSL mode, over the range chosen in the Input Range menu
Sets the green of the panel colour in RGB mode, or its saturation in HSL mode, over the range chosen in the Input Range menu
Sets the blue of the panel colour in RGB mode, or its lightness in HSL mode, over the range chosen in the Input Range menu
Menu — ColorMode — a heading over RGB and HSL, choosing whether the three inputs are read as red, green and blue or as hue, saturation and lightness; it comes up on HSL
Menu — Input Range — a heading over 0 - +10V (uni) and -5 - +5V (bi), setting the range all three inputs are read over; voltage beyond it is clamped
Note — the module comes up on -5 - +5V (bi) and on HSL, so a 0-10V modulation source reaches only the top half of each range until Input Range is changed
Note — dragging either edge of the module makes it wider or narrower, down to a minimum of 6HP
Note — an unpatched input holds its part of the colour at a fixed starting value, which is why the module opens violet
ColorPanel.notes: The three params carry the colour internally but have no widget on the panel, so no knob can be clicked. A note from an earlier pass said the ColorMode menu was dead; that is wrong for the installed 2.0.1, where ColorPanelFrame::step() reads colorMode and picks nvgRGBf or nvgHSL accordingly. The maker's own param names, 'Red or Hue', 'Green or Saturation' and 'Blue or Lightness', say the same thing.

lines: Thirteen buttons, each sending a gate from its own output while it is held down
Sends 5V from its own output while held down and 0V as soon as it is released, despite the manual saying 10V
Carries 5V while its button is held down, and 0V otherwise
MomentaryOnButtons.notes: The maker's README says the buttons send +10V; the code sets 5V. Thirteen inputs and thirteen lights are declared in the module but no widget is added for any of them, so none can be clicked or seen.

lines: Turns the computer keyboard's shift, ctrl, alt and super keys into gates
Shows whether that modifier key is held on the computer keyboard; clicking it changes nothing, because the real key state is written into it on every frame
Carries 10V while the left shift key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the right shift key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while either shift key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the left ctrl key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the right ctrl key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while either ctrl key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the left alt key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the right alt key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while either alt key is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the left super key, which is command on a Mac, is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the right super key, which is command on a Mac, is held down, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while either super key, which is command on a Mac, is held down, and 0V otherwise
Note — Rack's Computer Keyboard MIDI driver ignores keypresses while a modifier key is held, so playing notes on the QWERTY keyboard and holding shift at the same time does not work.
Note — the keys are read from Rack's own window, so nothing comes out while another application is in front
ShiftPedal.notes: The eight key switches are ordinary params, so a click does move them, but the widget's step() writes the live keyboard state into all eight every frame, so a click is overwritten before the next process call can use it.

lines: Sets one voltage and shows it at the same time as volts, VCO frequency, LFO frequency, LFO tempo, note name and cents
Sets the output voltage, -10V to 10V
Overwrites the knob with the voltage patched here, turning the module into a meter that reads that voltage in all six forms
Carries the voltage set by the knob, or the voltage at IN while something is patched there
Note — a value typed into any of the text fields sets the voltage: VOLTS, HZ, LFO HZ, LFO BPM and NOTE all write to the same one, and Command-A or Ctrl-A selects a whole field.
Note — HZ reads the voltage as a VCO pitch, with 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz; LFO HZ reads the same voltage as an LFO rate, with 0V giving 2Hz.
Note — NOTE takes names like C4, F#2 or Ab0, and negative octaves such as C-2; a flat is shown back as the equivalent sharp.
Note — the cents field shows how far the voltage is from the nearest exact semitone.
SpecificValue.notes: A second param, OCTAVE_PARAM, is declared but is never configured, never read and has no widget.

lines: Reads the value of whatever param or port the mouse is over, displays it, and sends it out as CV
Picks when the module reads what the mouse is over: always on on, only with shift held on w/shift, or never on off, where it starts, despite the manual saying it defaults to w/shift
Sets the range the scaled output is mapped into: -5/+5, 0/+10 or -10/+10, which it starts on
Carries the raw value of the param or port under the mouse, with no scaling, so it can go outside -10V to 10V
Carries the value under the mouse rescaled from that control's own lowest and highest values into the range set by the SCALED OUTPUT switch; a port is treated as running from -10V to 10V
Note — VALUE, MIN, MAX and DEFAULT show the hovered control's current value and its lowest, highest and default values, and TYPE says whether it is a param, an input or an output.
Note — the value is read at the screen refresh rate, around 60 times a second, rather than at the audio rate, so an audio signal tapped this way comes out heavily aliased.
Menu — Show Tooltip — floats a label beside the hovered control with its name, value and description; it is on to begin with
Note — the module comes up with its enable switch at off and reads nothing until that switch is moved to on or to w/shift
HoveredValue.notes: Two further params hold the raw and scaled values for the engine to read; neither has a widget. The README says the module defaults to w/shift, but the enable param is configured with a default of 0, which is off.

lines: Writes a CV into whatever param the mouse is over, so a knob or switch with no CV input of its own can be modulated
Picks when the module writes into the param under the mouse: always on on, only with shift held on w/shift, or never on off, where it starts, despite the manual saying it defaults to w/shift
Sets the range the input voltage is read over before it is mapped onto the hovered param's own range: -5/+5, 0/+10 or -10/+10, which it starts on; voltage beyond the chosen range is clamped
The voltage written into the param under the mouse, mapped from the range set by INPUT RANGE onto that param's lowest and highest values
Note — params on Inject Value itself are skipped, so its own switches cannot be driven this way.
Note — VALUE shows the value about to be written, and MIN, MAX and DEFAULT the hovered param's lowest, highest and default values.
Note — a switch fed a continuously varying voltage lands between its positions, and some modules misbehave on a value that is not one of the expected ones.
Note — the value is written at the screen refresh rate, around 60 times a second, rather than at the audio rate.
Note — the module comes up with its enable switch at off and writes nothing until that switch is moved to on or to w/shift
Note — with the switch at w/shift, a value is written only while a shift key is held down
InjectValue.notes: An output, DEBUG1_OUTPUT, is declared but has no widget and is never written. The README says the module defaults to w/shift, but the enable param is configured with a default of 0, which is off.

lines: Four channels that each hold the last voltage read at their input and go on sending it after the cable is pulled
The voltage to pass on and store; storing starts once it has moved away from 0V, and an input held at a steady 0V leaves the stored voltage in place
Carries the voltage at its input, or the last stored voltage while nothing is patched in, including one saved with the patch
Note — the text field below each pair of jacks is a label for that channel and is saved with the patch.
ValueSaver.notes: The four ports carry whatever is patched through them, so no family is claimed for any of them.

lines: Raises a gate once no trigger has arrived at its input for a set time, and drops it again as soon as one does
Each trigger here ends the idle gate and restarts the timer; when nothing arrives for the time set, the module goes idle
A trigger here restarts the timer without ending an idle gate that is already up
Patching a clock here takes the idle time from the gap between pulses; a pulse arriving with no event since the last one counts as idle, and the knob and time input are ignored
Sets how long with no event before the module goes idle, from 0 to 10 seconds
Adds to the knob to set how long with no event before the module goes idle, one volt per second, with its own voltage clamped to 0-10V
Carries the time before idle as a voltage, one volt per second and no higher than 10V; patch it to another Idle Switch's time input to give both the same setting
Sends a 10ms trigger at 10V at the moment the module goes idle
Carries 10V from the moment the module goes idle until the next trigger at the event input
Sends a 10ms trigger at 10V at the moment the idle gate drops, which is when a trigger reaches the event input
Any signal patched here goes to the when idle output while the module is idle and to the off idle output the rest of the time; it need have nothing to do with the event input
Carries the switched input while the module is idle, and 0V otherwise
Carries the switched input while the module is not idle, and 0V while it is
Note — the Time before idle display shows that time in ms and the Time remaining display counts down to going idle; with a clock patched, Time remaining stays at 0.
IdleSwitch.notes: An output, FRAME_COUNT_OUTPUT, is declared but has no widget. The switched input and the when idle and off idle outputs carry whatever is patched in, so no family is claimed for them. One Schmitt trigger object is shared between the clock input and the event input, so with a clock patched the two interfere; the panel and manual do not mention it.
